package_info.package_manager: proprietary (commercial software, not public package manager)
package_info.package_versions: 2019.4 HF 5, 2020.2, 2020.2 HF 1 (and others released between March and June 2020)
package_info.why_malicious: The SolarWinds Orion software was compromised during its build process, resulting in the injection of a backdoor into distributed, digitally signed updates. This allowed attackers to gain persistent, covert access to thousands of organizations globally, bypassing traditional security controls and code integrity checks.

execution_context.file_location: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll (compiled binary, source code injected pre-compilation)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code checks if it is running in the expected process, then beacons out to a hardcoded domain with system and environment information, awaits further commands, and executes them if received, enabling remote control and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code establishes covert network communication with an external domain, exfiltrates sensitive environment and system data, and allows remote command execution, all without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Orion DLLs should not contain code that initiates outbound network connections to unknown domains or executes remote commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may beacon to a central server for updates, but this is always documented, uses trusted domains, and is auditable.
key_indicators: Conditional execution based on process name
Stealthy network beaconing and command execution

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains access to SolarWinds build infrastructure (via credential compromise or insider threat).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code injection during build process

attack_chain.action: Malicious code (SUNBURST backdoor) is injected into the Orion Core BusinessLayer DLL during the build phase.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is signed and distributed as part of official software updates

attack_chain.action: Digitally signed, compromised Orion updates are distributed to customers via normal update channels.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is installed in thousands of customer environments

attack_chain.action: Upon execution, the backdoor code beacons to attacker-controlled domains, exfiltrates data, and awaits further instructions.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker achieves persistent, covert access to victim networks

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected outbound network connections from Orion process to avsvmcloud.com or similar domains
Orion DLLs containing code that checks process name and conditionally initiates network beacons
Remote command execution capabilities embedded in business logic DLLs
file_indicators: SolarWinds.Orion.Core.BusinessLayer.dll with unexpected code sections or hashes
Presence of digitally signed Orion DLLs with known malicious hashes
network_indicators: Connections to avsvmcloud.com and related C2 infrastructure
Beaconing patterns from Orion servers to external IPs/domains
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections from SolarWinds Orion processes to known C2 domains (e.g., avsvmcloud.com). Perform file integrity checks on Orion DLLs, comparing against known-good hashes. Analyze DLLs for suspicious logic such as process name checks and network beaconing. Use EDR/XDR solutions to detect post-compromise activity, such as remote command execution or lateral movement originating from Orion servers.
